title: Can I Send A Mass Email Campaign Using Brilliant Directories?
content:
Can I Send A Mass Email Campaign Using Brilliant Directories?
Link:
https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000558357
The built-in email system is designed for emailing active members who have requested to receive emails from the site. A common example would be sending a monthly newsletter to members who have opted in to receive updates.
The email system also sends transactional emails, such as new member signup notifications, credit card update notices, lead emails, and other system-generated messages related to member activity.
Sending mass unsolicited emails to Claim Listings or an imported contact list may be considered spam. This can violate email compliance laws, damage the sending reputation of your domain, and result in future emails being blocked or blacklisted.
In some cases, sending spam messages can also negatively impact other sites on the same server and may lead to account restrictions or termination with Brilliant Directories.

title: Email Forwarders
content:
Email Forwarders
Link:
https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000558373
Email Forwarders Not Supported
IMPORTANT:
The Email Forwarders functionality has been removed from our implementation of cPanel as of June, 2024.
Due to the way this functionality works in cPanel, it caused several issues for users. Some of these issue included:
Not all emails being forwarded properly based on the domain settings of the email sender and the receiver of the forwarded email
Sendgrid blocking emails from being sent to accounts hosted in cPanel, preventing the Admins of sites from getting notification emails
The domain reputation and reputation of the server being harmed when SPAM emails are forwarded through this system
While email forwarders can no longer be added or modified, any existing email forwarders will remain in place.  If an email forwarder needs to be removed from a site, please submit a ticket to our Support Team for assistance.
Recommendations to Replace Email Forwarders
The recommended alternative for using email forwarders is to use an email app that can send and receive emails from multiple email accounts in one place:
Gmail
Paid
Google Workspace
email accounts can connect to 3rd party email accounts to send and receive emails.  For this, the MX record would need to be pointed to Google workspace, for more information:
How To Change Email MX Records
Thunderbird
This is a free desktop email application from Mozilla, the makers of the FireFox browser. Thunderbird offers an app for Windows, MacOS, and Linux operating systems.
Apple Mail
Apple includes a free email client that can connect to 3rd party email accounts for all of their devices and operating systems.
Microsoft
Windows Mail
and
Microsoft Outlook
- Microsoft includes the Windows Mail and Outlook for Windows applications for free on devices using Windows 10 or newer. Both of these applications can connect to 3rd party email accounts.

title: How To Import Members Via CSV File
content:
How To Import Members Via CSV File
Link:
https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000558475
Overview
Importing members can be a bit of a tricky process due to the fact that all of the data entered must be simple, clean text (no formatting, line breaks, or other things that can break a CSV file), and the data must all be in the proper columns in order to import properly.
To start, here are some files that will help with understanding how the import process works:
Import template with ALL fields and explanations of each field
Import template with only the simple / basic required fields
Example of a completed import file with ALL fields
Example of a completed simple / basic import file
The template and example files that have "
ALL fields
" included show all of the different fields that can be filled out for a member during import.
However, not all imports will need to make use of all of these fields, so we also included a simple / basic version of each that has the most commonly used fields. Importing custom variables is also possible.
Downloading the File
Download one of the CSV import templates shown above.
In
row 1
of this file, one will see all of the headers required to import the data.
Make sure not to edit the spelling of any of these headers
, as doing so will cause the import to fail. In
rows 2 to 4
of this file, one will see an explanation of what kind of text should be added into each column (in the
listing_type
column, rows 2 and 3 show its only two values,
Company
and
Individual
).
Once the required content for each column is understood,
delete rows 2 to 4
from the spreadsheet (if they are not removed, the explanations will be imported as members of the site!)
Enter all of the member data into the correct columns
Delete any empty columns from the spreadsheet - for example, if no data is entered in the Twitter column, that column can be deleted from the spreadsheet completely. This will reduce the size of the import file and speed up the import process.
Add Categories to a CSV Import Spreadsheet
Categories go in 2 columns near the right side of the spreadsheet (columns AM and AN in the template with ALL fields) - "
profession_name
" and "
services
":
Top Categories
Under "
profession_name
" put the Top Level Category for the listing to be imported into. For example, if we were doing this for the Local Dessert Shops Directory then I could add “
Ice Cream Shop
” in this column.
The Membership Plan Settings also allow to pre-assign the Top level category to all profiles in that membership plan. For more information on how to do this, refer to
step 2
in the following
article
.
Sub Categories + Sub-Sub Categories
In the "
services
" column, add a comma-separated list of
Sub Level Categories
and
Sub-Sub Level Categories
one would like the listing added into.
For example, for the listing added into the Top Level Category “Ice Cream Shop”, one could add the Sub Level Categories "Ice Cream,Ice Cream Cake,Ice Cream Cupcake" (since these are all Sub Level Categories of “Ice Cream Shop” that apply to this listing). If one would like a listing imported into ALL Sub Level Categories under the Top Level Category it is being imported into (as designated in the profession_name column), then one could simply put "all" under the services column.
note that all of the Top Level Categories and Sub Level Categories entered into this spreadsheet must be spelled exactly the same as they are in the category structure in the Directory Planner.
If there are several sub or sub-sub-categories with the same name,
it is possible to select which specific sub-category to assign the member to.
1) Specify the sub-category first followed by this sign:
=>
2) Specify the sub-sub category, following this example:
sub level=>sub-sub level (Ice Cream Cake=>Vanilla Cake)
NOTE: Both Sub and Sub-Sub Level Categories should be entered under the "services" column, separated by a comma.
Helpful Tips
Automatically generated member URLs use the current name-formatting rules. Straight or curly apostrophes are removed, most other punctuation and spaces become hyphens, and underscores are preserved. For example, a member name of Ruby’s Clay Studio produces rubys-clay-studio in the name portion of the URL. These rules format the generated URL; the CSV file must still meet the import requirements in this article. See
How To Customize The Member Profile URL Structure
for the complete URL structure.
If any columns are blank in the import file, it is always best to delete the entire column. This is also mentioned above, but is a very common issue that people run into! For example, if none of the members which are going to import have any data for the "fees" column, it is best to delete this column entirely before import.
Some US zip codes begin with a zero or multiple zeros, which Excel and other spreadsheet programs sometimes remove automatically. Make sure all of the zip_codes are formatted as text and have all of the required 0’s at the beginning of the zipcode
If one is entering data for the logo, profile_photo, website, twitter, facebook, linkedin, or google_plus fields, be sure to use full URLs including the http:// (EG: http://www.google.com/image.jpg)
Make sure all listings have something entered into either the company or name field (or first_name and last_name fields) to insure that there will be a title for each listing.
Make sure to enter either
C
ompany
or
I
ndividual
into the
listing_type
field for each listing (Entering "Company" will make the company name more prominent in the listing; entering "Individual" will make the name of the person more prominent in the listing) *Our variables are case sensitive so make sure to capitalize the first letter for these.
Add the Top Level category for each listing into the profession_name column. Note that this must be spelled exactly the same as the category is spelled in the directory, or they will not import correctly. (See the section of this article above titled "How to Add Categories to a CSV Import Spreadsheet" for more tips)
(OPTIONAL) Add a comma-separated list of Sub Level Categories in each listing imported into in the services column (See the section of this article above titled "How to Add Categories to a CSV Import Spreadsheet" for more tips).
For best results, it is recommended to first create the Category Structure in your site before importing your members into these categories. For more information on how to create categories for members.
The fields "name" and " first_name + last_name" will create a conflict if they are both populated in the file.
Simply make sure that only "name" or "first_name + last_name" are populated. Either one will import the name of the listing successfully.
Import Existing Subscription & Billing Information
When importing members whose subscriptions are already established, their existing subscription information can also be included in the CSV file. This is especially useful when migrating members from another platform.
MPORTANT:
These fields are not required for standard member imports. However, if importing subscription information, both
subscription_start_date
and
billing_cycle
must be included together.
Stripe Customer ID
Field Variable:
stripe_customer_id
This field is intended for members who already have an existing Stripe Customer ID, such as when migrating members from another platform that was previously connected to Stripe. Adding the existing Stripe Customer ID allows it to be associated with the imported member.
Accepted format:
cus_
followed by alphanumeric characters only (eg:
cus_ABC123xyz789
)
The
billing_cycle
and
subscription_start_date
fields allow the Billing Cycle and Start Billing On information to be included during the member import, removing the need to manually create this subscription information for each imported member.
Subscription Start Date
Field Variable:
subscription_start_date
This field defines the subscription start date for the imported member. It is available for paid membership plans only and must be provided together with the
billing_cycle
field.
Accepted date formats:
YYYY-MM-DD (example: 2024-06-15)
YYYYMMDD (example: 20240615)
The website's configured date format (e.g. MM/DD/YYYY or DD/MM/YYYY)
The subscription start date cannot be more than one billing cycle in the past or more than 10 years in the future.
Billing Cycle
Field Variable:
billing_cycle
This field defines the billing cycle for the imported member's subscription. It is available for paid membership plans only and must be provided together with the
subscription_start_date
field.
The corresponding billing amount in the selected Membership Plan must be greater than 0. For example, if the billing cycle is Monthly, the plan's monthly amount must be greater than 0.
Available billing cycles depend on the billing options and prices configured for the selected Membership Plan.
Import the File
Navigate to the Search Members section of the admin. On the right side of the page, open the
List Actions
menu and select
Import Members via CSV File
. The import page opens; the numbers in the second screenshot below match the steps that follow.
The Import settings will allow the user to select the membership plan the new listings will belong to. This is required to begin the import.
A second option will allow the admin to determine the status of the listings upon import:
Set as ACTIVE Members
or
Set as NOT ACTIVE Members
.
An option to create a
Member Tag and assign a Tag Group
will show, the system will automatically fill out the tag name with the date and time of the import, the information can be edited and the tag can be assigned to any of the available Tag Groups:
The Advanced Options will allow the import to:
- Pass unique email checks
- Create new categories from the file if they have not been added to the admin yet.
- Geocode the users based on the location added to the CSV file. To use this function, add the "Pretty URLS API Key":
Set Up Pretty URLs with Google Maps
. A status line under the Geocode option shows whether the server key works, with a
Test
button to check it again and a button to add or fix the key (
Add a server key
or
Fix the server key
); a key Google refuses there is not saved.
- Auto import profile photo and logo images -
Member Images: Importing Members with Profile Photos, Logos & Cover Photos
"
Step 2. Upload CSV File Here
" will allow the user to select a CSV import file from the computer.
Once the file is selected, simply select "
Begin File Import
" for the upload to begin.
The
Import Members Data Map
will display on screen, listing each column header from the file with a preview of its first value and the directory property it will be imported into (1). When using the default import templates without any type of variable modification, we recommend to perform the import as is and click
Continue with Import
(2).
If the import file includes custom variables which may have been added to forms prior to the import, the same module will display them on the left side of the columns with an example of a value next to it. A column that does not match an existing property shows
Choose or create a property
in its
Directory Property
dropdown (1). Click that dropdown to choose the property the column should be imported into:
The dropdown lists the existing properties (1): every standard member field, plus any custom field that already has a value saved for at least one member. Should the new variable be missing from the list, click
Create new property
(2) at the bottom of the dropdown to create the variable name for a successful import:
Type the new property name and click
Add
(1) to add it to the dropdown. Use lowercase letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens: uppercase letters are changed to lowercase and spaces to underscores, and a name with any other character, or one already in the list, is not accepted:
Then open the dropdown again, type the new property name in the search box at the top, and click it to choose it for the column.
To leave a column out of the import, open its dropdown and click
Don't import column
(1):
Click
Continue with Import
. One last verification asks "Are you sure you want to run this Import Members File?": click
Yes, Continue
(1) for the file to be imported.
Important Note:
An error message titled
Import File Exceeds Member Limi
t will display in place of the Data Map when the number of members in the file plus the members already on the site is more than the site's member limit:
Once the import is completed a message is going to pop up to
Sync the members with Google Maps
:
"It is recommended to sync all newly imported members with Google Maps so they are searchable by location. Sync members now?" Click
Sync Members
(1) to open the geocoding page now, or
Cancel
to do it later.
To learn more information regarding member limits, refer to the article down below:
100,000 Member Limit Boost
Geocode Members
After importing the members, follow these steps in the link below:
Geocoding Members After A CSV Import
Import Profile Images (optional)
To complete the import of member images and logos, refer to the link below:
Member Images: Importing Members With Profile Photos, Logos & Cover Photos
For the Cover Photo to appear on the profile this Add-on must be active on the website
Profile Cover Photo
.
Get Personal Assistance
We understand that this can be a challenging process, even for some users that are more technically inclined. If one would prefer that someone on our team assists with the import of the members, we have Training Sessions covering importing members. Use the link below to purchase this service: Training Sessions
Important Notes
The files below should be downloaded to the computer and viewed in a spreadsheet application like Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets or another similar application.
Service Areas
can't be imported at this time, this might be something we add in the future.
The system checks default URL fields (website, booking link, social, etc) and only imports them if they’re in a valid URL format - otherwise, they’re skipped. Valid formats are: https://website.com or https://www.website.com.

services

one would like the listing added into.

note that all of the Top Level Categories and Sub Level Categories entered into this spreadsheet must be spelled exactly the same as they are in the category structure in the Directory Planner.
If there are several sub or sub-sub-categories with the same name,
it is possible to select which specific sub-category to assign the member to.

=>
2) Specify the sub-sub category, following this example:
sub level=>sub-sub level (Ice Cream Cake=>Vanilla Cake)
NOTE: Both Sub and Sub-Sub Level Categories should be entered under the "services" column, separated by a comma.
Helpful Tips
Automatically generated member URLs use the current name-formatting rules. Straight or curly apostrophes are removed, most other punctuation and spaces become hyphens, and underscores are preserved. For example, a member name of Ruby’s Clay Studio produces rubys-clay-studio in the name portion of the URL. These rules format the generated URL; the CSV file must still meet the import requirements in this article. See
How To Customize The Member Profile URL Structure
for the complete URL structure.
If any columns are blank in the import file, it is always best to delete the entire column. This is also mentioned above, but is a very common issue that people run into! For example, if none of the members which are going to import have any data for the "fees" column, it is best to delete this column entirely before import.
Some US zip codes begin with a zero or multiple zeros, which Excel and other spreadsheet programs sometimes remove automatically. Make sure all of the zip_codes are formatted as text and have all of the required 0’s at the beginning of the zipcode
If one is entering data for the logo, profile_photo, website, twitter, facebook, linkedin, or google_plus fields, be sure to use full URLs including the http:// (EG: http://www.google.com/image.jpg)
Make sure all listings have something entered into either the company or name field (or first_name and last_name fields) to insure that there will be a title for each listing.
Make sure to enter either
C
ompany
or
I
ndividual
into the
listing_type
field for each listing (Entering "Company" will make the company name more prominent in the listing; entering "Individual" will make the name of the person more prominent in the listing) *Our variables are case sensitive so make sure to capitalize the first letter for these.

in its

Create new property
(2) at the bottom of the dropdown to create the variable name for a successful import:

Add
(1) to add it to the dropdown. Use lowercase letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens: uppercase letters are changed to lowercase and spaces to underscores, and a name with any other character, or one already in the list, is not accepted:
Then open the dropdown again, type the new property name in the search box at the top, and click it to choose it for the column.

Don't import column
(1):
Click
Continue with Import

Yes, Continue
(1) for the file to be imported.

Import File Exceeds Member Limi
t will display in place of the Data Map when the number of members in the file plus the members already on the site is more than the site's member limit:

Sync the members with Google Maps

Sync Members
(1) to open the geocoding page now, or
Cancel

Geocode Members

Use the link below to purchase this service: Training Sessions

The files below should be downloaded to the computer and viewed in a spreadsheet application like Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets or another similar application.
Service Areas
can't be imported at this time, this might be something we add in the future.

content:
How to Override and Edit Default CSS stylesheets
Link:
https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000559709
The
Additional CSS
field applies custom CSS to every page of the website. It is useful for changing the header, the footer, the page background, or any other area that should look the same on all pages. CSS added here overrides the default CSS of the template.
Adding Custom CSS
Go to
Settings >> Design Settings
and open the
Custom CSS / HEAD
tab (1).
Add the custom CSS rules to the
Additional CSS
editor (2).
Check the status line under the editor (3). It should read
CSS looks valid.
(see
Live CSS Checker
below).
Click
Save Changes
.
Important: there is no need to include <style> tags.
Enter the CSS rules only. The website already places the contents of this field inside a style block.
To go back to the default styles, delete the CSS from this field and save. The styles reset to the template defaults.
NOTE:
Be careful when removing CSS from this field, as the custom CSS will be permanently deleted and cannot be retrieved.
Live CSS Checker
The Additional CSS editor checks the CSS while it is typed. A single missing closing brace (
}
) can break the layout of every page, because the custom CSS is placed in the same style block as the page’s other CSS, so the checker catches these mistakes before they are saved.
The checker reports in two places:
The status line
under the editor. It shows
✓ CSS looks valid.
in green when nothing is wrong, or a count of the problems found with the line number and description of the first one.
A marker in the editor margin
next to the line with the problem: red for an error, amber for a warning.
The clip below types a rule with a missing closing brace, shows the red error appear, then adds the brace so the status line returns to
CSS looks valid.
Errors (Saving Is Blocked)
Errors are problems that break the CSS that follows them. They are marked in red (1) and the status line turns red (2), for example
1 error (first on line 1: Unclosed rule — missing closing '}'.)
. The checker reports these errors:
Unclosed rule — missing closing '}'.
A rule or
@media
block was opened with
{
and never closed.
Unexpected '}' with no matching '{'.
There is an extra closing brace.
Unclosed comment — missing closing comment delimiter.
A comment was started with
/*
and never ended with
*/
.
While the Additional CSS has an error, clicking
Save Changes
does not save. A popup titled
Additional CSS has syntax errors
(1) names the line to fix, and the
Custom CSS / HEAD
tab opens so the error is in view. Fix the line, confirm the status line no longer shows an error, then save again.
The block applies to the whole Design Settings page.
The
Save Changes
button saves every Design Settings tab together, so an error in Additional CSS also stops changes on the other tabs from saving until it is fixed.
Warnings (Saving Still Allowed)
Warnings point at CSS that the browser will skip, but they never stop a save. They are marked in amber (1), and the status line ends with
saves still allowed
(2). The checker warns about:
Declaration outside a rule
, such as
color: red;
typed outside any
{ }
. The browser drops it and the rule after it.
Invalid value
for a property, such as
display: blok;
, or an
Unknown property
. The browser ignores that line.
Unclosed '(' or '['
, such as an unfinished
calc(
or
url(
. The browser ignores the CSS after it.
Warnings are worth fixing because the browser skips that CSS, but vendor prefixes (such as
-webkit-
), CSS custom properties (
--my-color
) and other valid modern CSS do not trigger them.
Bracket Matching
Placing the cursor next to a brace highlights the matching brace, which makes it easier to see which rule a closing brace belongs to. A brace with no partner is marked instead.
What the Checker Covers
Only the
Additional CSS
field is checked.
Additional HEAD Code
and
Additional Footer Code
are not checked and save as entered.
The checker runs in the admin editor. CSS that is already broken when the page loads is flagged as soon as the tab opens.

title: How Do I Cancel Payment Subscriptions - Orders
content:
How Do I Cancel Payment Subscriptions - Orders
Link:
https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000567728
An admin can end (cancel) a member's subscription from three places in the admin area. Ending a subscription stops all future payments for it and cancels its unpaid invoices. Each route asks for confirmation first and offers an optional box to record why the subscription is being cancelled.
Transaction History
The member's Payment History, Subscriptions tab
The member's Payment History, Transactions tab
Important:
Ending a subscription from the admin dashboard does not deactivate the member’s account. To completely remove a member so they no longer appear on the website’s front end, the site admin must manually update the member’s status.
Quick edit to modify member status
.
Transaction History
1. In the admin area, go to
Finance » Transaction History
.
2. Search for the member by name or ID in the
Search User Name or ID #
field (1 in the image below), then open the tab that holds the member's invoice:
Payments Received
,
Upcoming Payments
,
Past Due
,
Refunded
or
Stopped
(2).
3. On the invoice's row, hover over
Actions
and click
End Subscription
. The option only appears when the invoice belongs to an active subscription.
4. The
Confirm End Subscription
window opens. Optionally type the reason for the cancellation in the
Reason for cancelling
box (see
Recording a Reason for Cancelling
below), then click
Yes, continue
. Click
No, cancel
to close the window without ending the subscription.
The subscription ends, its unpaid invoices are cancelled, and no further payments are collected for it.
Member's Payment History: "Subscriptions" Tab
Subscriptions can also be ended from the member's own billing page.
1. Go to
My Members » Search Members
and find the member. Hover over
Actions
on the member's row and click
Payment History
.
2. Open the
Subscriptions
tab (1). On the subscription's row, hover over
Actions
(2) and click
End Subscription
(3).
3. The
Cancel Subscription?
window opens. Optionally type the reason in the
Reason for cancelling
box, then click
Yes, continue
. Click
No, cancel
to close the window without ending the subscription.
This is the same window that opens from
Actions » End Subscription
on the
Finance » Search Subscriptions
page. After the subscription ends, its row shows
Ended
, and any reason entered appears as a
Reason:
line in the
History
column.
Member's Payment History: "Transactions" Tab
The member's
Transactions
tab lists the same invoices as
Finance » Transaction History
, filtered to that member. Ending a subscription from here also cancels its unpaid invoices, including an unpaid invoice the system has already created for the next due date (invoices are created 13 days before the due date).
1. Go to
My Members » Search Members
, find the member, hover over
Actions
and click
Payment History
(as in the previous section).
2. Open the
Transactions
tab (1) and the tab that holds the invoice, then hover over
Actions
on the invoice's row (2) and click
End Subscription
.
3. The
Confirm End Subscription
window opens, the same one used on the Transaction History page. Optionally type the reason in the
Reason for cancelling
box, then click
Yes, continue
.
To refund a payment instead, open the same
Actions
menu on a paid invoice and click
Refund Payment
:
Recording a Reason for Cancelling
Both End Subscription windows include a
Reason for cancelling
box, so the admin team can keep a record of why each subscription was ended (for example, "Member asked to cancel by phone" or "Switched to an annual plan").
The reason is optional. Leaving the box blank ends the subscription exactly as before.
The box accepts up to 1,000 characters (
Limit: 1000 characters
is shown under it). Plain text only; emoji are not supported.
The reason is saved with the cancellation and appears in the
History
column of
Finance » Search Subscriptions
and the member's
Subscriptions
tab, as a
Reason:
line next to the
Ended
details.
The reason is also added to the activity notification the website records when an admin ends a subscription.
If the subscription is ended but the reason cannot be saved, the window shows
Cancelled, but the reason was NOT saved
. The subscription is still ended; only the reason is missing.
Read this article to learn how to create a new order (subscription):
How To Manually Bill A Member / Create A Subscription For A Member
.

title: Mandatory Fields For Member Imports
content:
Mandatory Fields For Member Imports
Link:
https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000568062
If there are any issues during the import process, it may be caused by one of the following mandatory fields missing.
Name or Company (name, company)
Field Variable: name, company
Include either the "name" or "company" fields. It is also possible to include both.
Name: Combines the first and last name.
Company: Company name
Listing Type (listing_type)
Field Variable: listing_type
Company: Will display the company name in search results
Individual: Displays the individual's name in search results (commonly used for medical or professional directories).
Country Code (country_code)
Field Variable: country_code
Two-letter
country codes
are assigned to each listing. Although only the country_code is strictly required, omitting the zip_code and city fields prevents accurate geo-coding, resulting in an incomplete user experience.
Profession Name (profession_name)
Field Variable: profession_name
Top-level categories associated with each member. This is the minimum required to have members import and display properly.
Subscription & Billing Fields
The following fields are optional for standard member imports. However, when importing existing subscription information, both fields must be provided together.
IMPORTANT:
Subscription and billing fields are optional and are not required for standard member imports. However, if importing subscription information, both
subscription_start_date
and
billing_cycle
must be included together.
Subscription Start Date
Field Variable:
subscription_start_date
Defines the subscription start date for an imported member on a paid membership plan. This field must be provided together with
billing_cycle
.
Accepted date formats:
YYYY-MM-DD (example: 2024-06-15)
YYYYMMDD (example: 20240615)
The website's configured date format (e.g. MM/DD/YYYY or DD/MM/YYYY)
The subscription start date cannot be more than one billing cycle in the past or more than 10 years in the future.
Billing Cycle
Field Variable:
billing_cycle
Defines the billing cycle for the imported member's subscription. This field must be provided together with
subscription_start_date
. The corresponding billing amount configured in the selected Membership Plan must be greater than 0.
Available billing cycles depend on the billing options and prices configured for the selected Membership Plan. The corresponding billing amount for the selected cycle must be greater than 0. For example, if the billing cycle is Monthly, the plan's monthly amount must be greater than 0.

content: Member Profile Analytics Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000619186 The Member Profile Analytics add-on is a click tracking tool, provides insights for admins and members with valuable data such as profile views, clicks to their website, visits to their social media profiles and member posts – all broken down by day, month and year. Use these statistics to show the members how they are analytically benefiting from the website. How To Get This Add-On Websites with the VIP Add-Ons Club automatically have this add-on available: Join The VIP Add-Ons Club Purchase Individually: Member Profile Analytics Add-On Enabling the Add-On Select which membership plan is allowed to view Profile Stats in Finance > Membership Plans : Click Edit to enable the statistics inside the plan settings: Open the Member's Dashboard tab: Scroll down to the option for "Enable Profile Statistics" and select the option that the admin wishes to have: Enable Only For Admin Enable For Member And Admin Disabled Tracked Links Here is a list of the links that the website tracks in the Profile Analytics for members. Member Profile Clicks Profile Visit Phone Number Member Website URL Member Social Media Links Contact Form (Send Message): counted once per submission, whichever option the form uses under What Happens After Form Submitted (Display Success Pop-Up Message, Display Success Alert Message or Redirect to Another Page). Private Chat Messages (first interaction) The option that decides what happens after a contact form is submitted is set per form in Toolbox > Form Manager, by clicking Edit Form Settings on the form. Contact Form submissions are counted with any of the three options in the What Happens After Form Submitted dropdown: Multi-Image Post Clicks Photo Albums Products + External Link (Web URL that will link visitors to more details) Digital Products Properties + External Link (Web URL that will link visitors to more details) Classifieds + External Link (Web URL that will link visitors to more details) Single Image Post Clicks Videos Articles Jobs + External Link (Web URL that will link visitors to more details) Events + External Link (Web URL that will link visitors to more details) Coupons + External Link (Web URL that will link visitors to more details) Audios Discussions Tracking Custom Links A custom link or button added to a member’s listing, such as a booking button that opens an outside booking service, can be tracked too. Its clicks are counted in Profile Analytics under a name chosen for the link. A tracked custom link needs two things in its HTML: the weblink class and a data-click-type attribute holding the name that should appear in the statistics: Copy Book a Visit To add a tracked link to a member’s listing: Go to My Members >> Search Members and open the member. Click Edit Status to open the Quick Edit window, then open the Advanced Options tab (1). Paste the link HTML into Listing Custom FOOTER Code (2), changing the name, address and button text as needed. Click Save Changes . Once the link has been clicked at least once, its name appears as its own column on the member’s Profile Analytics tab (1, 2): Rules for tracked custom links: The link must be saved on the member’s own record , for example in Listing Custom FOOTER Code . A click is only counted when a link with the same data-click-type name is stored on that member. Links added another way, such as through site-wide header or footer code or a widget, are not counted. Names can use letters in any language, numbers, spaces, hyphens and underscores, up to 64 characters. Upper and lower case are treated as the same name. Names containing combining marks (some vowel signs in scripts such as Hindi or Thai) are not accepted. Built-in statistic names cannot be used , such as Website , Phone , Profile Views , Contact Form , Facebook or Instagram , so a custom link never adds to a built-in count. The link address can be anything , including an outside website. A link that is not a full web address (such as #book or /contact-us ) still counts; the click is stored with the address of the profile page it came from. A link without data-click-type is not counted when it points somewhere other than the member’s own website or social media profile fields. Adding the weblink class alone is not enough. Test while logged out. As with profile views, clicks made by the website admin or by the member while logged in are not counted. Notes All page loads are counted. However, views generated by the profile owner while logged in, as well as views by the website admin, are excluded. Clicks won't be tracked if the page content is set to Members-Only Content , or if the member is inactive. Viewing Profile Analytics Admins can monitor profile analytics from the Admin Dashboard and Member Dashboard , including search result views, daily and monthly profile visits, and recorded clicks on social media and website links. Detailed insights are available when profile statistics are enabled for a membership plan. Admin Dashboard The admins will be able to see the amount of views in the member search results, as well as in the member's Profile Analytics tab (opened from Actions » Account Details) if the profile statistics are enabled for the membership plan : Top Views Dashboard Modules The admin dashboard shows three modules for this: Most Viewed Profiles (1), Most Viewed Posts (2) and Visitor Activity (3), each with its own date range. Admin Dashboard Modules Member Dashboard Also the admin can login as any member in that specific Membership Level, on the left sidebar look for Profile Statistics click on it and the profile views per month will be shown: Click on the month to check more detailed stats, it will display the views per day: Social media clicks and website link clicks will also be recorded and added to the report. They will not show up if no clicks have been registered. The Visual Chart can be placed anywhere in the Member Dashboard. For example, adding [widget=Bootstrap Theme - Account - Listing Statistics Chart] per Membership Plan under Member's Dashboard » Custom Dashboard Content » Dashboard Header Content : set the dropdown to Use Text Editor (1), paste the shortcode into the editor (2) and save the plan: Post Views Posts will display how many views they have received in total: Notes Currently, there is no Download Report functionality for this tool; the content is viewable only. Adding Stats to Emails Email variables make it possible to display the Stat numbers inside outgoing emails. This article outlines the format, shows the default variables available in the editor toolbar, lists all supported date options, and explains how to create custom variables. User Stats: Displaying Profile Statistics in Emails Using Variables Search Members Sorting Options Having this add-on active will show additional sorting options in the Search Members section in the admin dashboard. Members can be sorted by Most and Least views:

title: Predictive Keyword Search
content:
Predictive Keyword Search
Link:
https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000657865
Search functionality is a key element of any directory website… It’s how the users are able to find the information they need.
The Predictive Keyword Search add-on can help users find information on the website even faster. With this add-on, as a user begins typing their search term into the website’s search field they will instantly be presented with potential search results.
How To Get This Add-On
Websites with the VIP Add-Ons Club automatically have this add-on available:
Join The VIP Add-Ons Club
Purchase Individually:
Predictive Keyword Search Add-On
Enabling the Add-On
To customize the auto-suggest on the website please follow these steps:
Go to Developers Tools:
Click on Autosuggest Settings:
Auto-Suggest Settings
Rule Variable:
This is the variable that will be linked to the search box the admin would like to apply the auto-suggest rule to.
The admin can locate the current variable being used by hovering the mouse over the search box and inspecting the element. Here is a quick video that shows how to complete this.
These are the default options that we provide:
When any of the default options is being edited or created, they all have the same setting options:
Use a Class or ID:
It is always recommend to select "Class".
Enable Auto-Suggest After How Many Characters:
This is the number of characters a website visitor needs to enter before the auto-suggest starts to show options.
Maximum Auto-Suggest Limit:
The total number allowed to be shown. If there area total of 25 possible results, but the limit is 10, only ten lines will show(1 header and 9 results), respected the order that it was set in the "Select the features the admin would like to be searched in the autosuggest rule" section. Keep in mind that the number set here includes the heading of each section.
Example:
If the maximum Autosuggest limit is set to 2
It will show the Header and just one listing.
Auto-Suggest Rule Settings
Enable Listings:
This decides whether or not listings will appear in the auto-suggest. The same setting is available for all features and categories as well.
Limit:
The amount of listings that will display so long as the max limit has not already been reached.
Photo:
This allows the admin to decide whether or not a photo will display in the auto-suggest. We suggest turning this on for Listings and all features.
Link:
Turning this on will automatically take the visitor to the next page. Turning this off will auto-fill the box with that entry, but still allow the visitor to add a location. We suggest setting categories to "no" and the rest "yes".
Show Header:
The "Header" is the main title for that section. The following image shows three features that have "Show Header" as "Yes".
Location:
If "Yes" is selected, the location for that member or data post will show in the auto-suggest. In the image above, "Listings" have this set to "yes".
Details
: This will add a second line of information in the auto-suggest. The details vary on the item selected:
Listing Details = The top-level category
Sub-Categories Details = The top-level category. If it is a sub-sub, it will show the parent category (sub-level)
All Feature Details = They will show the name of the Feature. Some customers prefer to use this instead of the "Show Header" option.
Editing The Order
The auto-suggest also allows the admin to easily change the order of items being shown in the auto-suggest.
The highlighted modules are the ones active on the rule that's being edited:
In order to restore the settings back to default, click on the Restore Button:
This tool will reset
all
the settings to their default version and delete any updates the admin have completed so far.
To learn more about this add-on, please read this article:
How To Edit Keyword Search Autosuggest Settings For Member Searches

title: How Search Result Ordering and Distance Sorting Work
content:
How Search Result Ordering and Distance Sorting Work
Link:
https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000662041
Overview
The following explains three search result behaviors that are commonly misunderstood. Each section describes how the system is designed to work and why.
1 — Searching by State, Country, or Region Does Not Produce Distance-Sorted Results
When a visitor searches using a
state, country, province, or county name,
for example, "Texas," "California," or "United Kingdom", the system does not sort results by distance. This is by design.
Distance sorting only activates when the searched location resolves to a
specific point on a map,
such as a
city name
,
zip code
,
postal code
, or
street address
. These location types have a precise latitude and longitude coordinate, which the system uses as the reference point for calculating member distances.
⚠ NOTE — If Distance Sorting Is Not Appearing for City or Zip Code Searches:
If distance is not calculating correctly even when a specific city or zip code is searched, verify that the members in the results have been geocoded. Members without geocoded coordinates will not have distance values and will not sort correctly by distance, regardless of the location searched.
Reference:
How To Geocode Members
2 — Results Are Sorted by Distance from the Searched Location, Not the Visitor's Physical Location
When a visitor searches for a location, the system returns members sorted by their proximity to the
searched location,
not by their proximity to the visitor's current physical position.
For example, a visitor located in Chicago who searches for
"90210"
will see members sorted by their distance from the Beverly Hills area, not from Chicago. This is the intended behavior.
This design allows a visitor to search for businesses or listings near a hotel, a client's office, or any location other than their own. Sorting by the visitor's physical location instead would make location-based searching impractical for any use case where the visitor and the searched area are not in the same place.
3 — Members on Higher-Priority Plans with Service Areas Can Rank Ahead of Geographically Closer Members
When a Membership Plan is configured to allow members to select service areas, those members will appear in search results for their selected service area locations regardless of where they are physically located. If that plan also carries a higher search result priority than another plan on the site, its members will rank above geographically closer members on the lower-priority plan.
Example:
A member physically located in California and New York, as a selected service area. This member will appear in the New York search results. If that member's plan has a higher search priority than a member who is physically located in New York on a lower-tier plan, the California-based member will rank above them.
This behavior is the result of two deliberate configuration choices on the site:
The Membership Plan has
service area
selection enabled.
The Membership Plan has a higher
search result priority
than the plan being outranked.

After selecting a payment gateway, create an account with the chosen payment gateway if one does not already exist. Navigate to Finance » Payment Settings, where a list of available gateways is displayed. Click the "Add New Payment Gateway" drop-down and select the desired gateway.
NOTE:

Keep in mind that the payment gateway will use the Website Currency selected under
Settings » General Settings » Localization
.
Important Note:
When adding credentials for the Stripe gateway, there will be additional validation on each key field as the valid credentials should be between 25 and 255 characters, and the key cannot include dots (ex: ....).
In the "Secret or Restricted Key" field, it is possible to enter either a standard Secret Key (beginning with sk_) or a Restricted Key (beginning with rk_).

Link:
https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000673912
The following steps outline the steps members follow to upgrade to a higher membership level or downgrade from a paid to a free membership plan:
1. Click "Change My Plan" in the Member Dashboard:
2. Here, the members can select the preferred membership plan and click "Click to Continue":
3. The members will then be able to select which plan they would like to upgrade to:
4. The billing module will confirm the payment amount. The system will
not attempt to prorate
the upgrade price in any way, it will charge the full amount of the new membership plan (In this case, the Premium plan is $19.99) and will start a new subscription.
Example: If a member purchased a Basic Membership for $1 on 03/15/2021 and 15 days later (03/30/2021), they upgrade to the Premium Membership which is $19.99, the system will start a new subscription for $19.99 on 02/30/2021 and the old subscription for the Basic Membership will be canceled.
The system will not refund the unused portion of the old membership.  However, an admin of the site can issue a partial refund from the payment gateway account (Stripe, 2Checkout, Authorize.net, PayPal Payments Pro, etc), if necessary.
5. A success message will appear if the transaction is processed successfully.:
6. If the member is moved to a membership plan that does not have upgrade/downgrade options available, the
Change My Plan
button will no longer appear:
7. Under the billing section on the member dashboard, if the
Downloadable PDF Invoices
add-on is active on the site, the members can view or download their invoices.
From the Owner's Perspective
The transaction will appear in the member's "Transaction History".
*To locate this section, search for the member and click Actions » Payment History » Transactions tab:
The payment will also appear on
Finance
»
Transaction History
:

title: Members-Only Content
content:
Members-Only Content
Link:
https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000682638
Distributing information online has never been easier. But with technology comes new challenges, such as protecting the premium content or confidential information.
This add-on provides full control over who can access the website’s content by requiring designated “members” to log in before being able to view the premium and protected content.
How To Get This Add-On
Websites with the VIP Add-Ons Club automatically have this add-on available:
Join The VIP Add-Ons Club
Purchase Individually:
Members-Only Content Add-On
Enabling the Add-On
Some websites find it beneficial to only show the content of the directory to other members of the directory.  We have a very simple way available in order to make this sort of functionality active.
There are 2 main areas the admin can protect and set as MEMBERS ONLY:
Web Pages
/
Display Options / Members-Only Page
Member Posts
/ Always Show Content
Find out below how to activate these settings for different needs.
Web Pages
/ Display Options / Members-Only Page
A
login will be required to view the page selected.
Go to: My Content - Web Page Builder and Select the page that will only be available to members:
On the right sidebar settings, check the "Protect This Page" and select the Only Allow Members so non-members can not see this page. Finally, click on "Save Web Page". Next is
the option to select which members get to see the page:
Now select which type of members are allowed to see this certain page:
The pages that are already members only will have this show up:
Important Note:
If a page is "Members Only" by default the Advanced Option "Apply NoIndex, NoFollow" will always be selected, search engines can only crawl publicly available pages.
Member Posts
/ Always Show Content
A
login will be required to view the post selected.
Go to: CONTENT >> EDIT POST SETTINGS >> Select the member post
that will only be available to members:
On the first tab "General Settings" choose the option that best fits for the website:
No Selection
- This is the default option, it will show the complete content to everyone.
Protect Search Results
- This option will not allow members that do not have access to this feature see the results or the details of the post.
Protect Detail Pages
- This option will show the search results and on the member's profile but if they wanted to see the details of the post it will not allow them unless signed in.
Important:
The
Member Listings
Post Type only shows one option:
Protect Search Result Pages.
To protect the rest of the pages the Members Only options can be found in the Membership Plans section.
When a post is set to members only, they are easy to identify:
Member Listings
/ Profile Page / Contact Page / Review Page
The Member Listings Member's Only settings are available per Membership Plan, to find these settings go to:
Finance > Membership Plans > (select the plan you want to set up) > Edit > Search Visibility > Member's Only Access:
Protect Profile Page
-
This option will show the search results but it will not allow non signed-in members to see the member's profile page.
Protect Contact Page
- This option will make the contact page a members-only page, members will need to be logged in to contact a member within the website.
Protect Write a Review Page
- This option will make the submit a review option for a member's profile a members-only page.
NOTE: If the profile pages are protected, but the search results are available for non-registered users, the phone number will also be hidden from the search results to protect the member information on this page as well.
The phone number will also be hidden from search results pages for
Inactive
or

members

Google Maps API: Features, Functions, and Key Considerations
Link:
https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/5000682639
The Google Maps API plays an essential role in powering location-based features on Brilliant Directories websites. By integrating directly with Google’s mapping technology, it provides members and visitors with accurate, flexible, and dynamic location search options that go far beyond simple address lookups.
From handling multiple spellings and landmarks to displaying real-time map results and offering advanced geocoding controls, the API brings significant functionality to any directory site.
At the same time, there are important requirements and limitations to be aware of, ensuring site owners understand both the advantages and the boundaries of this integration.
Benefits
The API offers a range of benefits for website owners who connect their site to Google Maps, making it easier for members to find locations and access relevant map-based features.
One of the powerful parts of BD, as users generate content, or join from different locations; all the profiles pages and search result pages are all automatically created and dynamically populated.
Location Flexibility
Search for any type of location, including street addresses:
Landmarks
Search for landmarks:
Location Spelling
Search using different spellings of the same location (Montreal vs. Montréal), even using accents and other special characters:
Robust handling of misspellings / imperfect matches:
Map Display
Search results are displayed on a Google Map:
Additional Information:
»
Google Map Search Results Add-On
Geocoding
New manual geocoding module gives the website administrator full control over correcting the latitude and longitude assigned to each member:
Additional Information:
»
How To Geocode Members
Latitude and Longitude
Members will use Google Maps when filling out their profile information to provide an exact latitude and longitude for their listing (even if Google Maps does not recognize their written address):
Additional Benefits
Location auto-suggestions are lightning-fast, as they are delivered directly from the Google Maps API.
Location data is pulled in real time from the Google Map's location database, meaning your locations always use the latest location data available from Google.
Location searches are automatically tailored to your users' likely behavior. For example, if a user is located in India, the system will read their IP address and provide them with location suggestions that are most likely to fit their needs.
Gain unprecedented control over how searches behave on your site.  For example, choose between having bounding-box search results or radius search results for every type of location search. For example, if a user searches for "90210", you will be able to restrict results to the northeast and southwest points of that specific zip code, providing incredible local results, OR choose to provide results within a set radius from the center of that zip code.
Requirements
You must provide your own (free) Google Maps Javascript API key.
Getting an API key:
Google Maps Javascript API Key
Limitations
The auto-suggest module when users are entering location information has limited customization options. Since it is directly returning results from the Google Maps API, the suggestions provided are not editable.
Using the mouse wheel to zoom in and out on the map is not available for the integration.
For Kosovo, searches cannot be performed using the “bounds” search type. Only radius-based searches are supported. This limitation occurs because locations within Kosovo are not consistently recognized as cities or other locality types in the underlying data, preventing bounds-based queries from returning results. This limitation is due to how Google Maps classifies locations in the region.
Location search results cannot be strictly limited to specific geographic regions. Since the Google Maps API is built to return results intuitively, it will know where a user is located, and likely matches to their search are given precedence. If the search is ambiguous and could refer to several different locations, it will provide additional location suggestions, which CAN be controlled through your Admin settings.  However, the initial search a user enters may not provide results within your preferred countries if Google believes the search is most likely for a location outside of your preferred countries.
Most websites and applications may use the Google Maps API free of charge. However, if you consistently generate a high amount of traffic, you may be required to pay for additional usage of the API. If your site or application generates 25,000 or more map loads each day for more than 90 consecutive days, Google may contact you to upgrade from the free API. But don’t worry!  If you go over the limits, Google will not immediately shut off your API access or display error messages on your site.  And if you are generating more than 25,000 map loads per day consistently, your website is already a major success!
Places (New) API
To ensure more accurate searches, websites that use the Google Maps “
PLACES (NEW) API
”  require visitors to select an option from the dropdown suggestions. In the past, users could type free-form text and attempt a search without confirming a recognized location, which often led to incomplete or invalid results. With this update in place, the search will not continue unless a valid suggestion has been chosen, making the process clearer and more reliable for everyone using the site.
When a visitor tries to search without selecting a suggestion, a small banner appears at the top of the results with the message “
REQUIRED: Select Location
”.
Next to it, an exclamation point icon provides additional context when hovered over, displaying “
Please select a location from the suggestions dropdown to continue.
”
This approach makes it immediately obvious what action is needed and reduces confusion or errors during the search process.
Text Labels
The banner message and tooltip are both standard text labels in the system. This means they can be fully customized, translated, or removed from the admin area if desired. Editing these labels allows administrators to match the exact language or terminology used on their website.
Google Suggestion Require Text
Google Suggestion Require Text Popover
While removing the text is possible, it is not recommended since doing so would reduce clarity for visitors and may lead to repeated search errors. The default labels provide helpful guidance and are intended to create a smoother, more user-friendly search experience.
